note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Patient presenting with progressively worsening upper lip swelling and breathing difficulty after ingestion of prawn soup, concerning for anaphylaxis. Past history of asthma and peanut allergy noted.
- Urgent plan to call ambulance and administer antihistamines in view of suspected anaphylactic reaction; hospital referral and follow-up for allergy management advised.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Acute allergic reaction with progressive lip swelling and respiratory symptoms  
- Onset approximately 30 minutes after eating prawn soup. Lips initially tingling, progressing to significant swelling of upper lip. Patient reports increasing difficulty breathing and feeling dizzy.  
- Associated symptoms: sensation of throat closing, mild chest discomfort or difficulty breathing; no detailed chest examination findings documented.  
- Past similar episode approximately one year ago after curry; difficult breathing and swelling reported but management unclear.  
- Social history: occasionally eats out with friends; not documented if any recent allergen exposures beyond prawn soup.  
- Given history of peanut allergy and asthma, this is suspected anaphylaxis.  

Issue 2: Past medical history of asthma  
- Patient uses salbutamol inhaler regularly; no other inhalers reported.  
- No documented recent asthma exacerbation or details on asthma control.  

Issue 3: Peanut allergy with prior severe allergic reaction  
- History of childhood severe allergic reaction requiring unspecified injection and hospital attendance.  
- Patient takes intermittent antihistamines but specific medication names and dosing not documented.  
- No current antihistamines available at time of consult.

Medications:  
- Salbutamol inhaler, dose/route/frequency not documented  
- Occasional antihistamines (names and doses not documented)

Allergies:  
- Known peanut allergy

Past Medical History:  
- Asthma  
- Severe peanut allergy with prior anaphylaxis in childhood

Social History:  
- Lives alone but had a friend present at time of event  
- Social alcohol use noted (prior drunkenness at time of allergic reaction)  
- Occasionally dines out with friends

Preventative History:  
- Not documented

Physical Examination:  
- No vital signs documented  
- Clinical signs: progressive upper lip swelling; reported but not objectively examined respiratory distress and dizziness

Plan:  
- Immediate emergency action: ambulance called for suspected anaphylaxis  
- Administer oral antihistamines while awaiting ambulance  
- Advise hospital attendance for acute management including possible epinephrine administration  
- Recommend allergy specialist follow-up post-discharge to review allergy management and prescribing of epinephrine auto-injector  
- Advise patient to carry antihistamines and epinephrine device once prescribed  
- Follow-up call or appointment to reassess after hospital treatment  

Document_quality:  
- Allergy history and medication names partly unclear and not fully documented  
- No vitals or physical exam findings recorded  
- Communication clear; occasional patient distress and dizziness noted but audible  
- Conflict noted: patient initially mentioned sandwich, later corrected to prawn soup  
- No documented preventive care history or recent allergy review
